QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_25

question.text: The OECD DAC evaluation criteria, widely used in development-programme evaluation, include which of the following standard set?

answer.text: Relevance, Coherence, Effectiveness, Efficiency, Impact, Sustainability

explanation.text: The Logic: The OECD DAC evaluation criteria (updated in 2019) are: Relevance, Coherence, Effectiveness, Efficiency, Impact, and Sustainability. The original 1991 set had five criteria; Coherence was added in 2019. These criteria provide a globally recognised structure for development-programme evaluation. The Trap: Option 2 is financial-analysis terminology (liquidity/solvency/profitability). Option 3 is POSDCORB (a classical management framework). Option 4 is the AIDA marketing funnel. Only the DAC set fits development-programme evaluation. Note: The OECD DAC criteria are not enumerated in the cited Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook (January 2026) pages 127-128, which lists SIA impact-assessment parameters as Inclusiveness, Relevance, Effectiveness, Efficiency, Convergence or Coherence, and Sustainability. The framing above reflects general industry/international-development knowledge of the OECD DAC criteria.
